              words, the stress is on the syllable of the original word:
              artist = Oo (stress on the first syllable) remove  = oO  (stress on the second syllable)
              Here are some  more  examples.

               nouns and  adjectives Oo                        verbs  00

              Most  two-syllable nouns and  adjectives have stress on the first syllable, even if they don’t come
              from an original one-syllable word. For example,  ‘brother’ doesn’t come from  the original word
              ‘breth’, but it still has the stress pattern Oo.                                          =

              Note: However, there are a number of exceptions to this general rule, for example as/eep, mistake,
              machine, alone, which have stress on the second syllable.
   C  |       Most  two-syllable verbs have stress on the second syllable, even if they don’t come from an
              original one-syllable word. For example, ‘repeat’ doesn’t come from the original word  ‘peat’, but
                                         Dae                           nama       tha                      hae
              it still has the stress pattern (oO).
              Listen to this sentence: the verbs all have the pattern
         B37
              Escape to Scotland, forget about work, just relax and enjoy the scenery!

              Note: There are a number of exceptions to this general rule, for example cancel, copy and two-syllable
             verbs ending in -er and -en, e.g. answer, enter, offer, listen, happen, open, which all have stress on the
              first syllable.

         B38
              Some  words are both  nouns and  verbs. For example, record is a noun if you put stress on the
              first syllable, and a verb if you put stress on the second syllable. Listen to these examples. You
             will hear each word  twice, first as a noun and then as a verb.
              record  contrast   desert  export   object  present   produce   protest  rebel
        >
              Note: There is not always a change of stress in words that are both nouns and verbs. For example
              answer, picture, promise, reply, travel, visit always have stress on the same syllable.

              Note: The stress stays in the same place when we make longer words from these two-syllable nouns,
             adjectives and verbs. For example, in both happy (Oo) and unhappy (000), the stress is on the syllable
              happ, and in both depart (00) and departure (000), the stress is on the syllable part.
